sections.title: Habit and leaves
sections.text: Coffea liberica is a coffee tree native to western Africa and cultivated in tropical regions. It can reach about 18 m. Its large elliptic leaves are leathery with wavy margins; the flowers are white and fragrant.

sections.title: Fruits and comparison
sections.text: Ripe fruits are berries about 3–3.5 × 1–1.5 cm, usually containing two seeds that are processed and roasted for coffee. The tree habit, large leaves and fruits shown on the plate are consistent. Compared with Arabica and Robusta, Liberica can be notably taller, though size depends on cultivation.
